The Petitioner filed this petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 claiming compensation from the respondents due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of Petitioner's case, is that on 18-11-2023 at about 7.20 p.m, he was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53/HG-2217 on Doddadenahalli-Gerapura Gate and reached near Gerapura Gate, wherein the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-76/AV-7251 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life, came at high speed from opposite direction and dashed against the Petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident.
As a result of forced impact Petitioner was fell down and sustained several grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to MVJ Hospital for first aid, then he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, during hospitalization X-rays were taken which revealed that the petitioner had sustained (1) right humerus shaft comminuted fracture open type 3B with radial nerve palsy, (2) Right foot 2 nd toe proximal phalanx shaft fracture and 5th proximal phalanx base fracture and other injuries and underwent right arm wound debridement with right elbow spanning ex fix on 19-11-2023 under BPB, right radial nerve exploration and repair with sural nerve graft on 22-11-2023 under BPB + SA and was discharged on 25-11-2023 with an advice of regular follow up treatment and medication.

Even now petitioner is under regular follow up treatment by spending huge amount of Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment, food, transport and other charges.

It is further stated that the injuries sustained in the said accident, the petitioner is not able to lift or carry any weight, unable to drive or ride any vehicle, cannot do his day to day activities as earlier to the accident, not able to wear the dress properly and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings, since the injuries caused are permanent in nature.
4.
It is also stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 37 years and was working as Electrician and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

He is the only earning member in the family, the entire family was depending upon the petitioner's income and he lost his earnings and by causing lot of pain, shock, mental agony and financial difficulties.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-76/AV-7251.
Hence, the Hosakote Traffic Police registered a case against driver of said vehicle under Crime No.369/2023 U/Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.

6. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal and hence he was placed Ex-parte.
Respondent No.2/Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

7. Respondent No.2 in its written statement contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition and it liable to dismissed in limine.
This respondent has not admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-76/AV-7251, but, restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, the rider of the motorcycle and driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid D.L. and the owner of the Lorry did not posses valid FC and permit to the said vehicle as on the date of the accident, hence, terms and conditions of insurance policy were violated.

Further denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.

8. On basis of the Pleadings and materials, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what quantum and from whom?
3.
Whether order or award?
9. In order to prove the case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and further got marked 3 documents as Ex.P.17 to 19.
The plaintiff got examined the Orthopaedic Surgeion of HOSMAT Hospital, Bangalore as PW.2 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.P.14 to P.16.
On the other hand, the respondents have not examined any witnesses or produced any documents on their sides.
10. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

For the following reasons, this Tribunal answer the above Issues as under:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
 REASONS 12. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner filed this petition against respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

13. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief affidavit of examination in chief he had reiterated the averments of petition and got marked 13 documents and further got marked 3 documents as Ex.
P.1 to 13 and P.17 to 19

. Ex.P.1 is the Copy of F.I.R.
Ex.P.2 is the Copy of Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Copy of IMV report, Ex.P.5 is the copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P.6 is the Copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act,
Ex.P.7 is the Copy of reply to the Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet, Ex.P.9 is the Copy of Aadhaar Card.

Ex.P.10 is the notarized copy of DL, Ex.P.11 are the photos and receipt,
Ex.P.12 is the Medical bills, Ex.P.13 is the Medical Prescription, Ex.P.17 and 18 are the discharge summary and Ex.P.19 is the Medical Prescription.
14. Dr. Krishan Prasad, the Orthopaedic Surgeon, Hosmat Hospital, is examined as PW.2 and got marked three documents as Ex.P.14 to 16.
Ex.P.14 is the Inpatient records, Ex.P.15 is the Out patient records, Ex.P.16 is the X-rays.

15. The respondent No.2 has contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and denied about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident and contended that the insured vehicle is falsely implicated in the petition.
But, to prove this contention, the Respondent No.2 had not adduced any evidence and also not produced any document on its behalf.

16. On perusal of Ex.P.3-Spot Mahazar and Ex.P.8- Charge Sheet it appears that, on the date of accident, driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-76/AV-7251 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and dashed the petitioner's motor cycle and caused the accident.
As a result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, the Hosakote Police have filed charge sheet against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
But, there is no any material to hold that, there is a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

17. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 took contention that the respondent No.1 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but the respondent No.2 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.2 has not proved that the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

19. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1 the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 the copy of mahazar, Ex.P.4 the copy of IMV Report, Ex.P.5 the copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 the copy of 133 notice, Ex.P.7 the copy of reply to 133 notice, Ex.P.8 the copy of charge sheet, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-76/AV-7251.
Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner claimed the compensation amount of Rs.25,00,000/-.
As per Ex.P.5 wound certificate the petitioner sustained degloving injury of middle 1/3rd arm, lacerated wound over right temporoparietal region.
The doctor had opined that the injury is grievous in nature.

Hence, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for amount of Rs.60,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
21. The petitioner had produced medical bills, which are marked as Ex.P.12 and P.19.
The respondents not denied the medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.4,55,011/- under the head of medical expenditure.
22. As per Ex.P.17 and P.18 discharge summaries the petitioner took treatment at HOSMAT Hospital, Bengaluru from 19-11-2023 to 25-11-2023 and also from 24-02-2024 to 27-02-2024 i.e., 11 days.

Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.11,000/- under the head Transportation, food, Nourishment and conveyance charges.

23. To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined Dr. Krishan Prasad,
Orthopaedic Surgeon, Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore as PW-2.
In the chief-examination affidavit the doctor deposed that, on 19-11-2023 the petitioner went to him for assessment of disability.
On examination the petitioner has sustained wound debridement right arm with elbow spanning external fixation was done (The radial nerve was cut with a gap).
On 22-11-2023-Radial nerve exploration and nerve grafting (with sural nerve from the foot) was done and diagnosed on 26-02-2024 removal of external fixation was done.
Result that the right humerus has gone for non-union with stiff right shoulder right elbow hand and right wrist with stiffness with pain and severe stiffness of the right wrist and right hand.
The right wrist drop (radial nerve palsy) has not recovered and his wrist is stiff in a position of flexion.
He cannot make a fist.
His right upper limb is totally nonfunctional and he has become a left hander.
The patient is wearing a humerus brace and a wrist brace and an arm pouch.

Assessment of disability on 26-09-2024, the patient says the problem that he was doing farming and electrician work before the accident and now he is not working, his right shoulder, wrist and right elbow are painful and stiff and has no grip of right hand and is unable Shivakumar D C vs Suresh Settu on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154339215/
5 to make a fist, unable to lift the right wrist upwards and he has pain in his right arm, he is unable to lift weights and has total inability in writing, typing, overhead activities combing, brushing and changing clothes, buttoning and eating.

sentences.text: He is unable to ride or drive a vehicle and he is unable to grasp objects with his right hand and he has become a left hander because his right hand is totally non- functional and his right wrist cannot be raised upwards.
The doctor assessed the total upper limb disability at 81% and that of to the whole body of the petitioner at 27%.
In the cross-examination doctor had stated that, he is not the treated doctor, he examined the petitioner only for disability assessment.
However by considering the nature of the injury and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal took the disability of the Petitioner at 20% to the whole body.

24. It is contended that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was doing Electrical work by self employee and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. and due to accidental injuries he is not able to carry on his work as before the accident.
The petitioner had not produced any document to prove his income and avocation.
This accident occurred in the year 2023.
In present days the coolie worker get Rs.500/- per day.

However by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal taken the monthly income of the Petitioner at Rs.16,000/-.
25.
As per Ex.P.9 and 10 Notarized Copy of Adhar Card and D.L. date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 30-06-1986.
Therefore, age of the petitioner is taken as 37 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 15 which comes as follows:
Rs.16,000 x 12 x 15 x 20% = Rs.5,76,000/-
Hence, this Tribunal award Rs.5,76,000/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
26.
The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medicine for further treatment.
In the chief- examination affidavit the petitioner deposed that, the doctor has advised him to undergo few more surgery in future for which he has spend huge amount.
The PW.2 doctor deposed in the chief affidavit that, the petitioner needs bone grafting and plating right humerus and corrective surgery for wrist drop and which will cost of Rs.3.5 lakhs.
In the Cross examination the PW.2 admitted that he has not given document to show that the petitioner required future treatment.
However, by considering the age and nature of injury and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head future medical expenses.
(Which does not carry any interest).

27. The petitioner stated that, prior to the accident he was doing electrical work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to attend the work and facing financial difficulties.
The petitioner had not produced any documents to prove his income and avocation.
This accident occurred in the year 2023.

However, by considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.

The Petitioner sustained grievous injury as shown in the wound certificate.
The petitioner was doing his own business and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

29. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount Pain and sufferings Rs. 60,000/-
Medical expenses Rs. 4,55,011/-
Transportation, Nourishment, 11,000/-
Conveyance and attendant Rs.
charges.

Loss of future income on 5,76,000/-
account of Permanent disability

Towards future medical Rs. 50,000/-
expenses Loss of income during laidup Rs. 30,000/-
period.

Towards loss of amenities of life Rs. 30,000/-
 Total Rs. 12,12,011/-
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,12,011/-.
30.
Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
(Excluding the future medical expenses) and not more than that.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
31. Liability:-
As already observed above, respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-76/AV-7251.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay Shivakumar D C vs Suresh Settu on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154339215/
7 compensation to the petitioner.

entities.text: Shivakumar D C vs Suresh Settu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the respondent No.2 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.12,12,011/- with interest @ 6% p.a. (Excluding the future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly  and severally liable to pay  compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.2 being  Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.

After deposit, the entire compensation amount along with interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification (As the petitioner has incurred huge amount towards medical expenses and also he has to incur some expenses towards future medication).
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
